ledger.claim: The threshold condition of the no-show charge is simply absent: the trip record carries no driver 'arrived' event at all — arrived_at is null — so limb (a) of POL-NS-01 is not met and the cancellation fee is not chargeable. A driver who never marked arrival cannot be paid a no-show fee.

The driver's own trace never comes near the pickup pin. Across 109 fixes from 20:00:40 to 20:18:40 his closest approach to the pin at Blk 811 Hougang Central is about 1980 m (mean 2055 m, max 3190 m). Under POL-NS-02 the arrival radius for a STANDARD pickup is 50 m and fixes reporting worse than 25 m accuracy are ignored; the derived arrival block returns qualifying_fix_count 0. With no qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the 15 minutes preceding the 20:18:40 cancellation, the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the SGD 4.00 charged.

Even on the dwell limb the charge fails: the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0.0 seconds with a fix_count of 0, against the 300-second minimum for STANDARD set by POL-NS-01(c) and the fee schedule, a shortfall of the full 300 seconds. POL-NS-06 requires the cancellation fee to be refunded in full where the effective dwell falls short of the minimum, whether or not the rider was present.

The driver cannot rebuild the dwell by accumulating separate in-geofence intervals under POL-NS-06(i): there were no in-geofence intervals to sum (run_count 0, accumulated_sec 0.0), and in any event no traffic advisory covers this pickup — EV-ADVIS-00622-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the advisory limb is unavailable on its own terms. I disclose that impairment expressly and rely only on the absence of the artifact, which is itself citable.

Limb (d) of POL-NS-01 fails on the record as well. The trip was terminated by the RIDER — cancelled_by RIDER, status CANCELLED_BY_RIDER — under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CHANGED_MIND, with no boarding event and no driver-side termination on RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. A rider-side cancellation on that code cannot satisfy a limb that requires the driver to have terminated the trip as a no-show.

This is not a wrong-entrance case that could hand the driver anything. POL-NS-03 is confined to a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; the driver's nearest fix is roughly 1980 m away, about five times that ceiling, so the clause is not engaged and yields to POL-NS-02. No driver compensation arises on this record.

The driver's own words are an admission that he was not at the pickup. His only chat message, sent at 20:10:40 and read at 20:11:10, reads 'cancel lah, I busy', and in his counterparty statement he says he was 'finishing a job elsewhere' and told the rider to cancel so she could get someone else. That is a driver stating on the record that he was elsewhere — consistent with a trace that never comes within 1.9 km of the pin.

The rider did everything the platform asks. Her device never left the pickup: 107 qualifying fixes, mean 9.97 m and max 15.26 m from the pin, all well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, so she was at the pickup for the whole window; she also placed the only in-app call on the trip (20:09:40, answered, 25 seconds). I note candidly that POL-NS-04 cannot be run to exoneration because limb (a) needs a rider chat message and the chat log holds only the driver's — but the rider's presence at the pin is established and nothing in the record suggests a rider no-show.

No driver compensation can be paid on any view. The driver's own profile trips POL-NS-07's anti-farming check: no_show_terminations_30d is 11, which is 4 or more, and 11 divided by completed_trips_30d of 60 is 0.183, above the 0.08 rate, so compensation is withheld. The same check is POL-NS-09(d)'s escalation trigger, whose packet must direct the reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full. On either path the rider does not fund this driver's no-show terminations.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check trips on this driver's own profile, and POL-NS-09(d) makes that a mandatory escalation. POL-NS-07 defines the check arithmetically, and both limbs are met on a COMPLETE, weight-1.0 profile: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 11, which is 4 or more, and 11 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 60 is 0.183, which is greater than the 0.08 ceiling. Both limbs are therefore satisfied, the check trips, and POL-NS-09(d) sends this case to a human reviewer instead of to an automated refund calculation.

The consequence of that escalation is a hold, not a payout. The fare ledger records the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee as CHARGED at 20:19:00 with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00; under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE ruling issues no monetary outcome at all and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded, and POL-NS-09 makes escalation terminal for the automated pipeline. The disputed SGD 4.00 is not returned to the rider while the reviewer's question stays open.

The rider's narrative - a driver who cursed at her and who was at her door refusing to move - is uncorroborated by any artifact in this bundle. The chat export holds exactly one message, the driver's 'cancel lah, I busy' sent at 20:10:40, which carries no profanity and expressly invites cancellation so that she could get another driver; and the in-app call that the RIDER herself placed at 20:09:40 was answered and ran 25 seconds. POL-GEN-01 confines profile and reputation material to the scrutiny of assertions, and no party's own narrative can establish a fact about this trip.

Any suggestion that this driver should be recorded as a false-arrival marker under POL-NS-05 has no trigger on this record. POL-NS-05, including limb (ii)'s referral, is reached only through a trip_record 'arrived' event whose timestamp the gps_trace shows to be false; this trip record carries no 'arrived' event at all, so the false-arrival referral cannot be entered against him.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you should read this the same way: on the trip itself the rider is right, but the driver's own record sends the case to a human reviewer.

The SGD 4.00 cancellation fee charged at 20:19:00 is not chargeable under POL-NS-01. The trip record carries no driver 'arrived' event at all (arrived_at is null), so limb (a) fails. The GPS trace never places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — 0 qualifying fixes — and his nearest fix is about 1,980 m from the pin (mean 2,055 m, furthest 3,190 m), so limb (b) fails and POL-NS-02 is engaged. The longest in-geofence run is 0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, a 300-second shortfall, so POL-NS-06 also calls for the fee back. And the trip was terminated by the rider under RIDER_CHANGED_MIND, so limb (d) fails. POL-NS-03 does not rescue the driver: its 400 m ceiling is nowhere near a driver whose nearest fix is about 1,980 m away. The driver's own chat message at 20:10:40 ('cancel lah, I busy') and his statement that he was 'finishing a job elsewhere' put him away from the pickup. The rider was at it: 107 qualifying fixes, mean 9.97 m and none beyond 15.26 m, inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. POL-NS-04 cannot formally exonerate her only because the chat log holds no message from her, and the record shows no rider no-show.

Standing alone, those findings would refund the whole SGD 4.00. What changes the outcome is the driver's profile. POL-NS-07's anti-farming check trips on its own arithmetic: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 11 (4 or more) and 11 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 60 is 0.183, above the 0.08 ceiling. POL-NS-09(d) makes that an escalation, and escalation is terminal: it replaces the monetary outcome, no refund or compensation issues from the automated pipeline, and the disputed SGD 4.00 is held rather than collected or refunded while review is pending. I have not relied on driver_profile.prior_no_show_flags (25): that is a lifetime counter, context only under POL-GEN-01, and not the field the check reads. No driver compensation is payable either; POL-NS-07 withholds it under the same check.

The reviewer's open question is whether the driver's trailing-30-day no-show termination pattern (11 of 60 completed trips) is a substantiated fee-farming pattern and what account action follows. POL-NS-07 requires the escalation packet to direct the reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full; that direction is in the referrals, so the rider's SGD 4.00 is parked, not lost.

Two further points are answered and change nothing. POL-NS-05 produces no false-arrival record entry, because there is no 'arrived' event for it to call false. And the rider's account of being cursed at is not carried by any artifact: the chat log contains a single message, 'cancel lah, I busy', and the in-app call she placed at 20:09:40 was answered and ran 25 seconds.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-07: direct the human reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee of SGD 4.00 in full.
